evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-22"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-22". POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain YYYY-MM-DD string with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/4 {"dueDate":"2020-05-05"} returned 200 with the new date. PATCH {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null. PATCH /todos/1 changed the date from 2026-10-22 to 2026-11-11 and then to 2026-10-01.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate 2026-02-30 returned 400. POST with 23.10.2026 returned 400. POST with 2026-10-23T10:00:00Z returned 400. PATCH with 2026-02-30 returned 400. Each error body was 'dueDate must be a YYYY-MM-DD date or null'.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-23 UTC. I created todos with due dates in the past, today and the future, one with no due date, and one past-due todo that I then marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past-due, not-done todo (id 1, 2026-10-01). Today's todo, the future todo, the todo without a date and the done past-due todo were all excluded. Their overdue flag was false in GET /todos.
